k: A veteran S.H.I.E.L.D. agent
st: In season 1, Garrett is unmasked as the Clairvoyant, a HYDRA leader running Project Centipede.
Coulson destroys Garrett with an Asgardian weapon.

k: A S.H.I.E.L.D. specialist
st: In season 1, Ward is revealed as a HYDRA mole loyal to John Garrett.
Ward is caught by S.H.I.E.L.D. after Garrett falls.
In season 2, Ward escapes and leads his own war on S.H.I.E.L.D. with Kara Palamas.
In season 3, Coulson kills Ward on an alien planet.

k: An ancient Inhuman wearing Grant Ward's body
st: In season 3, Hive returns to Earth in Ward's body and bends Inhumans to his will.
Lincoln flies Hive into space, and both die in the blast.

k: A recruiter in a flower dress
st: In season 1, Raina recruits powered people for Centipede and HYDRA.
In season 2, Raina becomes a thorny Inhuman with visions and is killed by Jiaying.

k: A billionaire mining magnate
st: In season 1, Quinn builds a gravitonium machine and joins forces with Garrett.
A season 5 flashback shows Raina betraying Quinn, and the gravitonium swallows him.

k: A laid-off factory worker with sudden strength
st: In season 1, Garrett turns Mike into the cyborg Deathlok, using his son as leverage.
Mike turns on Garrett and walks away from HYDRA.

k: An Asgardian enchantress
st: In season 1, Lorelei escapes to Earth and enslaves men with her voice.
Sif takes Lorelei back to Asgard in chains.

k: A HYDRA scientist who never seems to age
st: In season 2, Whitehall leads HYDRA's hunt for the Obelisk.
Coulson shoots Whitehall dead before he can claim the Obelisk's power.

k: Whitehall's right-hand man
st: In season 2, Bakshi serves Whitehall and brainwashes HYDRA's prisoners.
S.H.I.E.L.D. captures Bakshi and hands him over to General Talbot.
Back with HYDRA, Bakshi dies leaping in front of a splinter bomb Simmons meant for Ward.

k: A S.H.I.E.L.D. agent brainwashed by HYDRA
st: In season 2, Kara wears a mask that copies faces and does HYDRA's work.
Kara joins Ward's war on S.H.I.E.L.D., and he kills her by mistake.

k: A man who takes on anything he touches
st: In season 2, Creel works for HYDRA until S.H.I.E.L.D. captures him.

k: Skye's volatile father, a doctor
st: In season 2, Cal seeks revenge on Whitehall and on S.H.I.E.L.D., which he blames for his wife's fate.
Cal kills Jiaying to save his daughter, and starts a new life with his memory erased.

k: Leader of a hidden Inhuman haven
st: In season 2, Jiaying, Skye's mother, leads the Inhumans of Afterlife.
Jiaying starts a war with S.H.I.E.L.D. and is killed by Cal.

k: An eyeless Inhuman who teleports
st: In season 2, Gordon serves Jiaying and carries Inhumans in and out of Afterlife.
In the season 2 finale, Gordon teleports behind Fitz and is impaled on the pipe in Fitz's hands.

k: Malick's Inhuman bodyguard
st: In season 3, Giyera moves objects with his mind and serves Malick and Hive.
Fitz kills Giyera with a cloaked gun aboard Hive's plane.

k: An Inhuman who charges objects with fire
st: In season 3, James joins Hive's cause.
In season 4, James returns as Hellfire, and Ghost Rider hands him over to S.H.I.E.L.D.

k: An anti-Inhuman hate group
st: The Watchdogs try to buy a HYDRA weapon from Colonel Ramon and test it on Yo-Yo.
The Watchdogs attack Inhumans across the country with Ivanov's money.

k: A Russian zealot who hates Inhumans
st: In season 4, Ivanov funds the Watchdogs and works with AIDA.
When his body is destroyed, Ivanov lives on as a head controlling android bodies.
In season 5, Ivanov returns with Hale's alliance, until Yo-Yo throws him out a window and he dies.

k: A US senator who fears Inhumans
st: In season 4, Senator Nadeer works with the Watchdogs against Inhumans.
Ivanov sends Tucker Shockley to test her with Terrigen, and Shockley turns Inhuman and explodes, killing Nadeer.

k: A corrupt Colombian police colonel
st: Ramon, the officer who killed Elena's cousin, tries to sell a HYDRA weapon to the Watchdogs.
When a Watchdog fires the weapon at Yo-Yo, its beam hits Ramon and kills him.

k: Robbie Reyes's uncle, a scientist
st: In season 4, Eli uses the Darkhold's science to make matter from nothing.
Ghost Rider drags Eli away through a portal.

k: A scientist obsessed with transhumanism
st: In season 4, Radcliffe builds AIDA and the Framework.
Radcliffe dies inside the Framework as it is erased.

k: An android assistant built by Radcliffe
st: In season 4, AIDA reads the Darkhold and traps the team in the Framework, ruling it as Madame Hydra.
AIDA becomes human as Ophelia, and Ghost Rider destroys her.

k: A Kree overseer of the last humans
st: In season 5, Kasius rules the humans of the Lighthouse in a ruined future.
Kasius loses his hold on the Lighthouse and dies fighting S.H.I.E.L.D.

k: Kasius's Kree enforcer
st: In season 5, Sinara enforces Kasius's rule with deadly flying spheres.
Sinara is killed in battle with S.H.I.E.L.D.

k: A US Air Force general
st: In season 5, Hale secretly works for HYDRA's remains and an alien alliance.
Hale's schemes collapse, and she is killed.

k: Hale's daughter, raised as a weapon
st: In season 5, Ruby, raised by HYDRA, cuts off Yo-Yo's arms.

k: An alliance of alien powers
st: In season 5, the Confederacy offers to protect Earth in return for Inhumans and gravitonium.

k: A US Air Force general who distrusts S.H.I.E.L.D.
st: In season 5, Talbot absorbs gravitonium and sets out to save Earth his own way.
Daisy fights Talbot and kills him.

k: An alien hunter wearing Coulson's face
st: In season 6, Sarge hunts the Shrikes across worlds and stabs May.
Sarge dies in the season 6 finale.

k: A body-hopping alien
st: In season 6, Izel jumps between bodies to open a gateway for her kind.

k: Androids from a fallen homeworld
st: In season 6, Chronicom Hunters come to Earth looking for a way to save their people.
In season 7, the Hunters chase S.H.I.E.L.D. through time to wipe it from history.
S.H.I.E.L.D. stops the Chronicom fleet in the final battle.

k: A Chronicom predictor
st: In season 7, Sibyl guides the Chronicom Hunters through time.
Sibyl is destroyed in the final battle.

k: Gideon Malick's brother
st: In season 7, Nathaniel joins the Chronicoms and gains Inhuman powers.
Nathaniel dies in the final battle.

k: A young Inhuman with a grudge
st: In season 7, Kora, Daisy's lost sister, joins Nathaniel Malick.
Kora breaks with Malick and fights at Daisy's side.

k: A Soviet spy ring
st: In season 1, Leviathan steals Howard Stark's deadliest inventions.
Peggy stops Leviathan's gas attack on New York and captures its leader, Fennhoff.

k: A Soviet psychiatrist
st: In season 1, Fennhoff hypnotizes Howard Stark to drop Midnight Oil gas on New York.
Peggy stops him, and he ends up in a cell next to Arnim Zola.

k: Peggy's friendly neighbor
st: In season 1, Dottie, a Leviathan assassin, befriends Peggy to spy on her.
In season 2, Dottie returns as a thief and spy, and she escapes after Peggy catches her.

k: A Hollywood star with a hidden genius
st: In season 2, Whitney absorbs Zero Matter and kills to gain power.
Peggy drains her of Zero Matter, and Whitney is locked in a mental hospital.

k: A Senate candidate in a secret council
st: In season 2, Chadwick covers up Zero Matter, until his wife Whitney kills him.

k: A Los Angeles mob boss
st: In season 2, Manfredi helps Whitney Frost, then helps Peggy stop her when Zero Matter consumes her.
Manfredi visits the broken Whitney in an asylum, still in love with her.

k: An AI that won its war and took the Infinity Stones
st: Ultron wins his war, takes Vision's body and all six Infinity Stones, and wipes out life in his universe.
He discovers the Watcher and starts destroying universe after universe.
The Guardians upload Arnim Zola's mind into him, and Zola takes over Ultron's body.
Ultron returns, comes to see that peace needs the living, and helps Captain Carter reach the Watcher.
He draws the Watchers' fire so the others can escape, and he is destroyed.

k: A HYDRA scientist living as a computer mind
st: Zola's mind, stored in a computer, is fired into Ultron and takes over his body.
He fights Killmonger for the Infinity Stones until Strange Supreme traps them both in a pocket dimension.

k: Erik Stevens, a soldier who saves Tony Stark
st: Erik Stevens saves Tony Stark in Afghanistan and wins his trust.
He betrays Tony, kills T'Challa, and makes himself king of Wakanda.
Recruited by the Watcher, he turns on the Guardians to take the Infinity Stones.
Strange Supreme traps him with Zola in a pocket dimension.

k: A grieving Doctor Strange who breaks every rule
st: To save Christine Palmer, Strange absorbs countless beings and grows monstrously powerful.
His fight against fate destroys his whole universe.
He joins the Watcher's Guardians and guards the trapped Killmonger and Zola.
He feeds heroes and villains to a forge to rebuild his lost world.
Captain Carter frees him from his inner demon, and he sacrifices himself to the forge.

k: A cosmic hoarder of rare beings
st: Star-Lord T'Challa's crew raids the Collector's vault and turns his own cages on him.

k: A grieving scientist hunting Avengers candidates
st: Grieving Janet, Hank Pym shrinks down and kills Fury's Avengers candidates one by one.
Fury and Loki expose him and end his killing spree.

k: Thor's brother, here to avenge his death
st: Loki brings an Asgardian army to Earth to avenge Thor.
Once the killer is caught, Loki stays and rules Earth.

k: HYDRA's leader, obsessed with the Tesseract
st: Red Skull uses the Tesseract to open a portal and summon a monster from another world.

k: Earth's heroes turned flesh-eating zombies
st: A virus from the Quantum Realm turns the Avengers into zombies that overrun the world.
Years later, zombified heroes such as Hawkeye and Okoye still roam the ruined world.

k: A zombified Scarlet Witch
st: Vision keeps the zombified Wanda at Camp Lehigh, feeding her the living.
Years later, as the Queen of the Dead, she commands the zombie hordes. She defeats the survivors, takes the Infinity Stones' power from the Hulk, and traps Kamala in an illusion.

k: A zombified Thanos wielding the Infinity Gauntlet
st: Zombie Thanos waits in Wakanda, wearing an Infinity Gauntlet missing only the Mind Stone.
In Wakanda, T'Challa knocks him into the molten vibranium core, destroying them both.

k: A zombified Carol Danvers
st: A zombified Captain Marvel locks Ikaris in an endless battle and attacks Kamala Khan's group.

k: A zombified king of Talokan
st: Zombie Namor attacks the survivors, and Kamala destroys him with her bangle.

k: The Asgardian king, turned by Wanda
st: Zombified, Thor kills Blade and the last defenders around the Hulk, until the Hulk's blast destroys him.

k: A Kree prisoner of the Nova Corps
st: Freed from prison by Nebula, Yon-Rogg betrays her and steals the code in her head for Ronan.
He turns on Nebula again in the final battle, and Korg kills him.

k: Irani Rael, leader of the Nova Corps
st: Nova Prime Irani Rael secretly plots with Ronan to hand Xandar over to him.
Exposed by Nebula, she tries to flee and falls to her death after a struggle with Nebula.

k: A Kree warlord set on taking Xandar
st: Ronan's Dark Aster closes in on Xandar to seize the planet.
Nebula turns Xandar's shield on his ship, and he dies when it is destroyed.

k: A boy with Celestial powers who falls to Earth
st: Trained by his father Ego, young Peter attacks Earth in 1988 with Celestial powers.
Peter turns on Ego, crushes his seedling and blasts his body apart.

k: A Celestial who sends his son to prepare Earth
st: Ego raises young Peter and sends him to Earth in 1988 to prepare it for his expansion.
He comes to Earth himself, but Peter destroys his body, and Ego lives on as his planet, vowing revenge.

k: A disgraced weapons maker out for revenge
st: On Christmas Eve, Hammer raids Avengers Tower to steal a vial that will give him great power.
Happy Hogan, turned into a purple brute by Bruce Banner's blood, stops him with Darcy Lewis.

k: The ruler of Sakaar and host of its death race
st: The Grandmaster keeps the stranded Tony Stark on Sakaar and makes him race in his deadly Grand Prix.
In the chaos of the race, a melt stick turns him into a puddle, and Valkyrie takes over Sakaar.

k: A Red Room leader with a living weapon
st: Melina sends a brainwashed Steve Rogers in the Hydra Stomper armor to bring her Captain Carter.
Steve flies the Stomper into the Red Room, and Melina is caught in the blast.

k: A war machine piloted by a mystery soldier
st: The Hydra Stomper, piloted by a brainwashed Steve Rogers, attacks Captain Carter's allies.
Free of the Red Room's control, Steve flies the Stomper into its base, and his body is not found.

k: A conquistador hunting the Fountain of Youth
st: Gonzolo leads Spanish soldiers into Mohawk lands to claim the Fountain of Youth for Queen Isabella.
Kahhori returns with the people of the Sky World, defeats his conquistadors, and he dies in the battle.

k: The tyrant king of a 1602 England
st: Crowned after Hela vanishes, King Thor orders Captain Carter arrested and rules by force.
He hands Peggy the scepter holding the Time Stone so she can stop the rifts.

k: A gamma kaiju that spawns an army of monsters
st: Bruce Banner's attempt to purge the Hulk with gamma radiation creates the Apex, a kaiju that spawns gamma monsters.
Years later it returns, and Banner's Hulk burns it to ash and absorbs its radiation.

k: A witch turned 1930s Hollywood star
st: Agatha becomes a movie star and gets Howard Stark to fund a film she plans to use for a ritual.
She plots to drain the Celestial buried inside Earth, but Kingo talks her out of it.

k: A masked outlaw ruling a ghost town in 1872
st: In 1872, Xu Xialing kills the original Hood and takes his dark powers for herself.
As the Hood, she rules a ghost town, and Kate Bishop hunts her for her family's deaths.
Shang-Chi refuses to fight his sister, and Kate Bishop kills her.

k: A Watcher who puts Uatu on trial
st: The Eminence puts the Watcher on trial for breaking his oath and moves to stop Captain Carter's team.
He merges with two other Watchers to erase Peggy's team, but her sacrifice strips him of his power.

k: A Peruvian commander and old friend of Coulson
st: Reyes turns on Coulson's team and seizes their plane to take the 0-8-4 for Peru, until the agents retake it.

k: A gravitonium expert kidnapped by Ian Quinn
st: Hall turns Quinn's gravitonium machine on the island, and Coulson shoots out the floor, dropping him into it.

k: A former S.H.I.E.L.D. agent pulling impossible heists
st: Akela steals for unseen masters through an implanted eye, until Fitz and Simmons remove it and S.H.I.E.L.D. takes her in.

k: A Centipede scientist working with Raina
st: Po runs Centipede's work and interrogates the captured Coulson, until the Clairvoyant has him killed.

k: A gifted student at the S.H.I.E.L.D. Academy
st: Donnie tries to sell his weather machine to Ian Quinn, gains ice powers, and ends up locked away by S.H.I.E.L.D.
Brainwashed by HYDRA, Donnie turns his ice powers on S.H.I.E.L.D., and Skye shoots him dead.

k: A Fridge escapee who drains energy
st: Daniels escapes the Fridge to find the cellist Audrey, and Coulson's team floods him with light until he dies.

k: Powered outcasts Cal gathers for revenge
st: Cal gathers Karla Faye Gideon, Angar and others to strike at S.H.I.E.L.D., but Coulson, Bobbi and May subdue them.

k: A young Inhuman girl in Bahrain
st: In a Bahrain flashback, young Katya controls the minds of everyone around her to kill, and May shoots her dead.

k: A hulking Inhuman who hunts other Inhumans
st: In season 3, Lash hunts and kills new Inhumans, and is revealed as May's ex-husband, Andrew Garner.
Lash breaks Hive's hold on Daisy, and James kills him with a burning chain.

k: Baron Strucker's son
st: In season 3, Werner joins Ward's HYDRA and tries to kidnap Andrew Garner, who turns into Lash and drives him off.

k: Alien hunters who follow Sarge
st: In season 6, Jaco, Snowflake and Pax follow Sarge across worlds hunting Shrikes, and clash with S.H.I.E.L.D.

k: A nightclub owner dealing in stolen goods
st: Raymond sells Howard Stark's stolen formula to Leet Brannis, and a Leviathan assassin kills him.

k: A silent buyer of Howard Stark's stolen inventions
st: Brannis buys Stark's nitramene, and after Peggy captures him, Leviathan's Sasha Demidov kills him.

k: A hitman tied to Calvin Chadwick
st: Hunt kills for Chadwick's cover-up, until Whitney Frost, angry at his mess, absorbs him into Zero Matter.

k: A HYDRA spy inside Project Rebirth
st: Kruger attacks Project Rebirth for the serum, killing Erskine and Phillips and shooting Steve, until Peggy kills him.

k: Thanos's children, sent ahead to Earth
st: Ebony Maw and Cull Obsidian land on Earth, and zombies overwhelm them and turn them into the undead.

k: A warlord gathering the Infinity Stones
st: Thanos comes to Earth with five Infinity Stones, and Ultron, now in Vision's body, slices him in half.

k: Tony Stark's partner at Stark Industries
st: Killmonger exposes Stane as the man who paid for Tony's ambush, and Happy punches him as he tries to flee.

k: An arms dealer with stolen vibranium
st: Killmonger kills Klaue and Rhodey during a vibranium deal and frames Wakanda for both deaths.

k: The All-Father who banished his daughter Hela
st: Odin banishes a powerless Hela to Earth, then comes for the Ten Rings, and Hela and Wenwu defeat him.

k: The mystery client known as the Rook
st: Unmasked as the Rook who sold out Howard Stark, Stane attacks Bucky and the Red Guardian, and Bucky kills him.

k: The master of the Red Room
st: Dreykov orders the Winter Soldier to kill the Red Guardian, and Bucky returns to him claiming the job is done.

k: A zealot who has taken over Knowhere
st: Having trapped the Collector, Kaecilius takes Howard and Darcy's egg to offer to Dormammu, until S.H.I.E.L.D. breaks in.

k: The host of an intergalactic cruise
st: The Grandmaster invites Howard and Darcy aboard his cruise, planning to eat their newborn egg.

k: Leaders of a Norse pagan hate group
st: In season 1, Jakob and Petra use a piece of the Asgardian Berserker staff to hunt the rest, until Ward and May beat them.

k: Chan Ho Yin, a fire-wielding street performer
st: In season 1, Chan Ho Yin joins Raina's Centipede as Scorch, and May overloads his Extremis to kill him.

k: A Kree warrior hunting the Diviners
st: In season 2, Vin-Tak tries to kill Skye, until Bobbi wipes his memory with his own weapon and Sif takes him home.

k: A T.A.H.I.T.I. patient killing the others
st: In season 2, Derik hunts down fellow T.A.H.I.T.I. patients, until Coulson stops him and he is handed to the authorities.

k: A senator, Grant Ward's older brother
st: In season 2, Senator Christian Ward pushes a multinational move against S.H.I.E.L.D., then trades it for custody of Grant.
Grant tortures Christian into confessing his past cruelty, then kills him and their parents.

k: Grant Ward's HYDRA second-in-command
st: Kebo serves as Grant Ward's second-in-command in HYDRA, until Bobbi Morse kills him.

k: A Momentum Labs scientist turned ghost
st: In season 4, Eli Morrow's machine turns Lucy Bauer into a ghost, and she goes after him until Ghost Rider destroys her.

k: A Watchdog who turns out to be Inhuman
st: In season 4, Tucker Shockley turns Inhuman and explodes, killing Nadeer, until Daisy, Fitz and Simmons contain him.

k: Madame Hydra's partner in the Framework
st: In season 4's Framework, Fitz is the Doctor, leading HYDRA with Madame Hydra, killing Agnes and torturing Radcliffe and Daisy.
Radcliffe sends him out of the Framework, and the real Fitz wakes up remembering every terrible thing he did.

k: A junkyard boss on the Lighthouse
st: In season 5, Grill runs the Lighthouse junkyard and spies on the agents, until Flint kills him with his new rock powers.

k: A 1931 speakeasy doorman, Gideon Malick's father
st: In season 7, S.H.I.E.L.D. saves Freddy from the Chronicoms, and he shoots Koenig to deliver a serum component to HYDRA.
By 1976, with the Chronicoms' help, Freddy rushes Project Insight into being, until Deke kills him.

k: A War Department veteran serving the Council of Nine
st: In season 2, Vernon Masters does the Council of Nine's bidding, blocking the SSR and steering Jack Thompson.
Thompson hands Masters over to Whitney Frost, and she starts draining him with Zero Matter before she is interrupted.

k: A silent Leviathan assassin
st: In season 1, Leviathan's Sasha Demidov kills Peggy's roommate and Brannis, then goes off a cliff in a truck as its weapons implode.

k: A Ravager captain working for hire
st: Yondu steals Howard and Darcy's egg from the Grandmaster's cruise and delivers it to Kaecilius, who kills him.

k: The Grandmaster's chief enforcer
st: Topaz locks up Tony and Gamora on Sakaar, and Valkyrie defeats her during Tony's race against the Grandmaster.

k: A ruler of a broken Earth with a drone army
st: After the Emergence splits Earth, Quentin Beck seizes Stark Industries and rules the survivors with his Iron Federation drones.
Helped by the Watcher, Riri drains the nanites out of Beck's body, killing him and ending the Iron Federation.

k: A zombified Emil Blonsky
st: A zombified Emil Blonsky storms the North Institute with Okoye's horde for the Queen of the Dead.

k: A zombified Ava Starr
st: A zombified Ava Starr storms the North Institute with Okoye's horde, and Blade kills her.

k: A zombified Steve Rogers
st: A zombified Steve Rogers storms the North Institute with Okoye's horde, and Alexei kills him.
